q.t: How many independent measurements are needed to construct a unique quadrilateral?
q.e: A diagonal splits it into two triangles: the first needs 3 measurements, the second shares the diagonal and needs 2 more.

q.t: How many measurements are needed to construct a square?
q.e: All sides are equal and all angles are 90°, so one side (or one diagonal) fixes it.

q.t: How many measurements are needed to construct a rectangle?
q.e: The angles are all 90°, so only the length and the breadth are needed.

q.t: How many measurements are needed to construct a rhombus?
q.e: For example the two diagonals, or one side and one angle.

q.t: How many measurements are needed to construct a parallelogram?
q.e: Two adjacent sides and the angle between them; the opposite sides then copy these.

q.t: To construct a quadrilateral from 4 sides and 1 diagonal, you first draw:
o: A triangle using the diagonal and two sides
All four sides in a row
q.e: The diagonal and the two sides on one side of it form a triangle that can be drawn by SSS.

q.t: A diagonal divides a quadrilateral into:
q.e: That is why quadrilateral constructions are built triangle by triangle.

q.t: To construct a rhombus from its diagonals, we use the fact that the diagonals:
o: Bisect each other at right angles
q.e: Draw one diagonal, its perpendicular bisector, and mark half the other diagonal each way.

q.t: Which instrument is used to mark equal lengths as arcs?
q.e: A compass keeps a fixed opening, so every point on its arc is the same distance from the centre.

q.t: Every angle of a square measures:
q.e: Four equal angles share 360°.

q.t: Can a unique quadrilateral be constructed from just its four sides: 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm?
o: No — the shape can still flex, a fifth measurement is needed
No — the sides are too long
q.e: Four rods hinged at the corners can be squashed into many shapes. An angle or a diagonal is needed to lock it.

q.t: A quadrilateral has three angles 80°, 100° and 120°. Find the fourth (in degrees).
Can quadrilateral ABCD be constructed with AB = 4 cm, BC = 5 cm and diagonal AC = 10 cm?
o: Yes, if CD is long enough
q.e: △ABC cannot exist: two sides (4 + 5 = 9) must together be longer than the third (10).

q.t: A rhombus is constructed with diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm. What will each side measure (in cm)?
q.e: Half-diagonals 3 and 4 at right angles: 3² + 4² = 5².

q.t: A rectangle is constructed with sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What will its diagonal measure (in cm)?
To construct a parallelogram you need two adjacent sides and:
q.e: The included angle fixes how much the parallelogram leans.

q.t: A square is constructed with diagonal 6 cm. How far is each vertex from the centre (in cm)?
q.e: The diagonals are equal and bisect each other at right angles, so each half is 3 cm.

q.t: Can a quadrilateral have three angles of 110°, 120° and 140°?
o: No — they already add up to 370°
Only if it is a kite
q.e: The four angles must total 360°, and three of them alone exceed that.

q.t: A quadrilateral is to be drawn given 3 sides and the 2 angles between them. Is it unique?
o: Only if it is a square
q.e: Draw the middle side, the two angles at its ends, and mark the other two sides; joining their ends completes it.

q.t: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 6 cm, AD = 4 cm and ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to 180°.

q.t: Can a parallelogram be constructed with sides 5 cm and 7 cm and a diagonal of 13 cm?
q.e: The two sides and the diagonal must form a triangle, and 5 + 7 = 12 is less than 13.

q.t: A rhombus is constructed with side 5 cm and one diagonal 8 cm. What will the other diagonal measure (in cm)?
q.e: Half of 8 is 4. 5² − 4² = 9, so the other half-diagonal is 3 and the diagonal is 6.

q.t: A rhombus is constructed with diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. What will each side measure (in cm)?
q.e: Half-diagonals 5 and 12: 5² + 12² = 13².

q.t: A rectangle is constructed with one side 5 cm and diagonal 13 cm. Find the other side (in cm).
A quadrilateral is given by AB = 5 cm, ∠A = 60°, ∠B = 110° and ∠C = 90°. What is ∠D (in degrees)?
q.e: 360 − 260 = 100. (Note: one more side is still needed to fix its size.)

q.t: A square is constructed with diagonal 8 cm. What is its area (in cm²)?
q.e: A square is a rhombus, so area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 8 × 8 = 32.

q.t: How many measurements fix a unique trapezium (given which sides are parallel)?
q.e: Knowing two sides are parallel is itself one condition, so only 4 more measurements are needed instead of 5.

q.t: A kite is constructed with its shorter diagonal 12 cm long. The diagonals cross 8 cm from one end of the longer diagonal. Find the length of each of the two sides that meet at that end (in cm).
q.e: The longer diagonal bisects the shorter one at right angles: 6 cm each way. Each of those sides is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 6 and 8: 10 cm.

q.t: A quadrilateral ABCD has AB = 3 cm, BC = 5 cm, CD = 4 cm and DA = 7 cm. How many whole-number lengths (in cm) can diagonal AC have?
q.k: len([d for d in range(1,20) if 5-3<d<5+3 and 7-4<d<7+4])
q.e: From △ABC: 2 < AC < 8. From △ACD: 3 < AC < 11. Both together: AC can be 4, 5, 6 or 7.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (not a square) have — useful for checking a construction?
q.e: Its two diagonals. Folding along either should make the halves match.

q.t: A rhombus is constructed with side 6 cm and one angle 60°. Find its shorter diagonal (in cm).
q.e: The shorter diagonal and two sides make a triangle with a 60° angle between equal sides — equilateral.

q.t: How many different quadrilaterals can have sides 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm in that order?
q.e: Without a fifth measurement the frame can flex continuously through endless shapes.

q.t: A parallelogram has sides 8 cm and 6 cm and one diagonal 10 cm. Find the other diagonal (in cm).
q.e: 6² + 8² = 10², so the angle between the sides is 90° — it is a rectangle, and a rectangle’s diagonals are equal.

q.t: Quadrilateral ABCD has AB = AD = 5 cm, CB = CD = 12 cm and ∠B = ∠D = 90°. Find AC (in cm).
q.e: In right △ABC: AC² = 5² + 12² = 169.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A : ∠B : ∠C = 2 : 3 : 4 and ∠D = 90°. Find ∠C (in degrees).
q.e: The three share 270°: 9 parts of 30°, so ∠C = 120°.

q.t: A rectangle is constructed with diagonals 12 cm long crossing at 60°. Find its shorter side (in cm).
q.e: Two half-diagonals of 6 cm with 60° between them make an equilateral triangle, so the shorter side is 6 cm.

q.t: A rhombus has perimeter 40 cm and one diagonal 16 cm. Find the other diagonal (in cm).
q.e: Side 10, half-diagonal 8: 10² − 8² = 36, so the other half is 6 and the diagonal 12.

q.t: A parallelogram is drawn with both adjacent sides 5 cm and the angle between them 90°. It is a:
o: Rectangle that is not a square
Rhombus that is not a square
q.e: Equal adjacent sides make it a rhombus, and a right angle makes it a rectangle — so it is a square.

q.t: Which data does NOT fix a unique quadrilateral?
o: Three sides and two included angles
Two adjacent sides and three angles
q.e: Four sides alone leave the shape free to flex; the others each give five working measurements.

q.t: A quadrilateral has diagonals 10 cm and 14 cm that bisect each other. What kind of quadrilateral must it be?
q.e: Diagonals bisecting each other is exactly the test for a parallelogram. They are unequal, so it is not a rectangle, and we are not told they are perpendicular.
